info.title: Tripz Backend API
info.description:
Multi-panel travel-marketplace backend exposing Super Admin, Admin, Vendor, Client, and Marketplace surfaces.

**Response envelope** — every endpoint returns:
- Success: `{ success: true, message: string, data: object | null }`
- Error: `{ success: false, message: string, errors: object | array | null }`

**Auth** — all authenticated endpoints expect a JWT access token via `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Refresh tokens are delivered as an httpOnly cookie (web) and also in the JSON body (mobile / API clients).

**Account states** — vendors who submit KYC are immediately deactivated (`isActive=false`) and only re-activated when an admin approves or rejects their KYC. Login & refresh return `code: ACCOUNT_UNDER_REVIEW` while pending.

post.summary: Register a new account (customer or agent)
post.description:
Single endpoint with an **identical payload for customers and agents**. Business details (country, company name, etc.) are collected later via the **Vendor KYC** flow, not at signup.

- `role: "customer"` → maps to internal `CLIENT`
- `role: "agent"` → maps to internal `VENDOR` (kycStatus starts as `PENDING`)

`ADMIN` and `SUPER_ADMIN` cannot be self-registered. User is created with `emailVerifiedAt = null`, an OTP is emailed, and **no tokens are issued** — call `/auth/verify-email` then `/auth/login`.

**Response includes `otp` metadata** so the frontend can render an accurate countdown timer and resend-cooldown button.

example.message: Account registered. Please verify your email to continue.
An account with this email already exists.

500.description: SMTP failure — verification email could not be sent

example.message: We could not send the verification email. Please try again in a moment.

post.description:
Returns an access token (15 min) and a refresh token (7 days). Refresh token is sent both as an httpOnly cookie AND in the JSON body — web clients use the cookie, mobile clients use the body.

**Failure modes:**
- `EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED` (403) — re-sends OTP automatically.
- `ACCOUNT_UNDER_REVIEW` (403) — vendor submitted KYC, waiting for admin approval.
- `ACCOUNT_DEACTIVATED` (403) — admin disabled the account.

EmailNotVerified.summary: Email not verified — a fresh OTP has been sent

value.message: Email not verified. We have sent a new verification code to your inbox.
Your application is under review. We will email you once your account is approved.
This account has been deactivated. Please contact support.

post.summary: Sign in (or sign up) with a Google ID token
post.description:
Verifies a Google ID token, then:
- If a user already exists with the same Google ID → log in.
- If a user exists with the same email (but no Google ID) → link the Google account (provider becomes HYBRID) and log in.
- If neither exists → create a new account. `role` is REQUIRED in this case ("customer" or "agent").

Returns the standard token pair, same as `/auth/login`.

ExistingUser.summary: Existing Google account — role not needed

201.description: New account created and signed in

400.description: Missing role on first-time signup, or invalid token

post.description:
Reads the refresh token from the httpOnly cookie OR the JSON body. Rotates BOTH tokens (old refresh is revoked, new one issued).

Detects replay attacks: if the same refresh token is presented twice, ALL of the user's refresh tokens are revoked as a defensive measure.

refreshToken.description: Optional — mobile/API clients send here; web clients use the cookie instead.

400.description: Refresh token missing from both cookie and body

401.description: Refresh token invalid, expired, revoked, or replayed

403.description: Account state blocks refresh — same codes as `/auth/login`: `ACCOUNT_UNDER_REVIEW`, `ACCOUNT_DEACTIVATED`

post.summary: Revoke the current refresh token + clear cookie
post.description: Idempotent — succeeds even if no token is presented. Always clears the refresh cookie.
Consumes the latest active OTP. After verification the user must call `/auth/login` separately — no tokens are issued here.

post.description: Generic-shape response (does not reveal whether the email exists). Subject to a `OTP_RESEND_COOLDOWN_SECONDS` rate limit per user. Response always includes `otp` metadata so the frontend can render the countdown — even on the generic branch.

Please wait 45s before requesting another code.

post.description: Generic-shape response regardless of whether the email exists (prevents account enumeration). Response includes `otp` metadata for countdown rendering.
On success, ALL existing refresh tokens for the user are revoked (any attacker still holding a stolen token is locked out). A confirmation email is sent.

post.description:
Generic file-upload endpoint. The backend forwards the file to Cloudinary and returns the public URL. **No database writes happen here** — caller stores the URL elsewhere (e.g., includes it in a later KYC submission).

Files are organized in Cloudinary as: `tripz/<purpose>/<userId>/<timestamp>-<filename>`.

file.description: Max 5 MB. Allowed: image/jpeg, image/png, image/webp, application/pdf.

post.description:
Public endpoint — accepts anonymous submissions from the marketing site. If a valid Bearer token is sent the lead is linked to that customer; otherwise it's stored with `customerUserId = null`.

**Hybrid data model**: `destination`, `email`, `phone`, `budget` are stored as top-level indexed columns; **everything else** (departureCity, travelDate, duration, adults, children, hotelCategory, etc.) is bundled into a single `requirements` JSONB field.

Leads land as `status: PENDING_REVIEW` and only appear on the marketplace after admin approval.

post.description:
Approves the KYC AND re-activates the vendor's account in one atomic transaction. A confirmation email is sent to the vendor.

Requires `kycStatus = SUBMITTED`.

Rejects the KYC, re-activates the vendor's account so they can log in and fix issues, and sends a rejection email with the reason.

Requires `kycStatus = SUBMITTED`. Vendor can resubmit — the next submission will deactivate the account again until re-reviewed.

get.summary: Get current vendor's KYC status & data
get.description: Returns kycStatus, the full KYC payload (if submitted), and every verified document so the frontend can resume a partially-filled wizard.

post.description:
Final step of the KYC flow. Persists company-level fields and flips `kycStatus → SUBMITTED`.

**Side effects on success:**
- `User.isActive` is set to `false` (vendor will be locked out after the current session expires).
- All refresh tokens are revoked.
- Vendor appears in the admin review queue.

Requires the vendor to have already verified PAN via `/vendor/kyc/verify/pan` first (third-party verified).

400.description: Validation failed, terms not accepted, or KYC already approved/under review

403.description: KYC already approved or already submitted

post.description:
Performs a real-time PAN check. In STUB mode (no `SUREPASS_TOKEN` set), returns success for any well-formed PAN.

Creates / updates a `VendorKycDocument` row with `thirdPartyVerified=true` on success.

post.summary: Start Aadhaar verification — initiate DigiLocker session
post.description: Hits Surepass `/digilocker/initialize` and returns a DigiLocker SDK URL. The frontend opens this URL (popup or full redirect); the user authenticates on DigiLocker (UIDAI OTP handled there). DigiLocker redirects back to the URL configured in `SUREPASS_REDIRECT_URL`. The frontend's callback page then calls `/aadhaar/complete` to pull the verified data.

example.message: DigiLocker verification initiated. Open the redirect URL to complete it.

422.description: Aadhaar number malformed or Surepass rejected the initiation

post.summary: Finish Aadhaar verification — fetch verified data from Surepass
post.description: Called by the frontend AFTER the user finishes authentication on DigiLocker (typically from the callback page that DigiLocker redirects to). Backend pulls the verified Aadhaar details from Surepass `/digilocker/get-aadhaar` using the parked `client_id` and marks the document as third-party verified. No OTP is sent — DigiLocker owns the OTP step end-to-end.

sessionId.description: Returned from /aadhaar/initiate; persists across the DigiLocker redirect (frontend stores in localStorage).

422.description: DigiLocker session still pending or expired

get.summary: Browse active leads in teaser mode
get.description:
Returns active leads (`status = ACTIVE`). For leads the vendor has NOT yet unlocked, `email` and `phone` are returned in masked form (e.g., `mo****@example.com`, `**********1332`). For leads they HAVE unlocked, full contact details are returned.

Requires APPROVED KYC.

403.description: KYC not approved or vendor account deactivated

post.summary: Unlock a lead — debits the vendor's credit wallet
post.description:
Atomic transaction:
1. Verify lead is `ACTIVE` and the vendor hasn't already unlocked it.
2. CAS-reserve a slot (`unlockCount < maxUnlocks`).
3. CAS-debit the wallet (`balanceCredits >= priceInCredits`).
4. Write a `DEBIT_LEAD_UNLOCK` ledger row with balance snapshot.
5. Create the `LeadAssignment` row.
6. Flip lead to `EXHAUSTED` if we consumed the last slot.

Any failure aborts the whole transaction — slot reservation and wallet debit can never desync. After success, the response includes the **fully unmasked** lead with real email/phone.

example.message: Lead unlocked. Contact details are now visible.

409.description: Lead no longer claimable (already unlocked, exhausted, or not ACTIVE)

value.message: You have already unlocked this lead.
This lead has just been fully claimed.
This lead is no longer available.

bearerAuth.description: JWT access token issued by `/auth/login` or `/auth/google/login`.

Unauthorized.description: Missing, malformed, or expired access token

Forbidden.description: Authenticated but role not allowed for this endpoint

errors.description: Either a structured object with a `code` field, or an array of validation issues, or null.

OtpMetadata.description: Metadata returned alongside any endpoint that sends an OTP — lets the frontend render countdown timers and disable resend buttons accurately.

password.description: Must include uppercase, lowercase, and a digit.

token.description: Google ID token (JWT) obtained from the frontend's Google Sign-In flow.

role.description: Required only when creating a brand-new account.

companyType.description: Accepts verbose UI labels like "Proprietorship Firm" or canonical enum values like "PROPRIETORSHIP".

VendorKycListItem.description: An item in the admin KYC list view — vendor profile plus their KYC payload, documents, and the linked user.

budget.description: Empty string accepted (treated as null). Otherwise numeric INR amount.

LeadTeaserView.description: Lead as returned to vendors on the marketplace feed. `email` and `phone` are masked when `isUnlocked = false`, full when `isUnlocked = true`.

email.description: Real email if unlocked; otherwise masked (e.g., `tr****@example.com`).

phone.description: Real phone if unlocked; otherwise masked (e.g., `********1332`).

lead.description: Fully unmasked lead — vendor paid for it.
